data.title: Chat: the AS-27 close()-clears-timer guard is vacuous — deleting clearInterval leaves the suite green

data.to:
From the AS-27 QA review (qa-priya, 2026-09-03), finding F1.

The test "stream: AS-27 — close() clears the loop poll timer" proves nothing. Mutation M4 deleted the clearInterval(loopPoll) call outright and all 255 tests stayed green, because close() empties the streams set first, so a leaked timer fans out to nobody and no assertion can see it.

The BEHAVIOUR is correct — the timer is cleared, and loopPoll.unref() means the process exits either way. This is a guard defect, not a bug: the assertion cannot fail, which is exactly the vacuous-pass shape CLAUDE.md requires guards to be proven against.

Fix: one test that samples process.getActiveResourcesInfo() either side of close() and asserts the timer count drops. Priya deliberately did NOT author it — writing an assertion and then verifying it herself is the conflict the review gate exists to prevent, so this needs a different author.

Acceptance: the new test goes RED when clearInterval(loopPoll) is deleted, and the mutation is demonstrated (not assumed) on a scratch copy.

data.body: Orchestrator (tick watcher:93997, loop tick 18): backlog -> in_planning, second lane beside the AS-73 review. AS-81 (the non-hanging harness this task's mutation demo was held for) merged last tick as c841c90, so the hold is released. Next by age in the Chat set after AS-74, which stays deferred until AS-73 merges (same personnel/roster seam). Planner: cto-owen as tech lead.

Plan written (cto-owen, tech lead, tick watcher:93997). DECIDED: the observable is NOT process.getActiveResourcesInfo() — loopPoll is unref()'d (server.js:650) and on node v24.13.1 getActiveResourcesInfo() reports [] for an unref'd interval (two-line experiment, recorded in the plan; _getActiveHandles() likewise 0). Chosen instead: t.mock.method(globalThis, 'setInterval'/'clearInterval') installed before createChatServer, record the four Timeouts the constructor arms (613/630/664/695), assert close() passes every one of them to clearInterval by identity, cardinality 4 asserted first. Zero deps, zero production diff, real timers (mock calls through), house precedent in watcher-main.test.js:450 (AS-82) so compose parity is already demonstrated. Probe in scratchpad/agent-cto-owen/AS-80-mock-probe/ proves a module-internal bare setInterval is seen by the global mock and a deliberately leaked timer reads as exactly 1. Rework the line-449 case in place (new name, AS-25 scaffolding kept, vacuous tail deleted): host count stays 480 (master e5de119 measured 480/0). M1 = delete clearInterval(loopPoll) (occurs once, line 1074), predicted exactly {T1} red, 479/1, whole suite. M2 = delete clearInterval(heartbeat), narrowed to --test-name-pattern 'AS-80' because the heartbeat is ref'd and the AS-25 case at line 322 leaks it and wedges the runner (pre-existing, not fixed here — noted as an omission, QA may file). LEFT OUT: a timers injection seam on createChatServer (rejected: one consumer, bypassable by a bare global call); any server.js edit at all. Branch feat/AS-80-close-clears-every-interval. Implementer: developer-lena (self-contained low; Marcus wrote the AS-27 stream tests). Reviewer: qa-ruben — Priya filed the finding and must not certify its fix; M6 probes named in plan section 10.

Implementation done (developer-lena). Commit f15d810 on feat/AS-80-close-clears-every-interval — one commit, diff = 1 file (apps/chat/test/stream.test.js, +37/-9), zero production change.

FINDINGS FIRST (outside the criteria list)

F-1 — AC-7's compose expectation is stale arithmetic, not a defect in this change. Observed: host 480 pass / 0 fail (31 test files) and compose 480 pass / 0 fail, and the two runs execute the IDENTICAL 480-case set — I extracted and diffed the full name lists (480 vs 480, zero names differing in either direction; scratchpad/developer-lena/AS-80/diff-names.mjs). The plan's 478 is AS-82's receipt taken on the AS-82 branch at 9d32a0c, two merges before this branch's base, paired with a host number measured at e5de119. The true host-minus-compose delta on this branch is 0. AC-7's "delta must equal master's 2" cannot be satisfied and should be re-derived; the reviewer should re-measure rather than take my number.

F-2 — the branch base is behind master and misses the AS-73 code merge, so no count in this comment matches master's. `git rev-list --left-right --count feat/AS-80-close-clears-every-interval...master` = 1 / 8, and `git branch --contains d815848` lists master only. Master's host count today is 486; this branch's is 480, and AS-73 (d815848) accounts for the 6 — it added cases in org-chart.test.js, personnel.test.js and the new roster-parity.test.js. Consequences: the number to expect after the --no-ff merge is 486, and a post-merge 480 would mean the merge dropped AS-73. No conflict risk — AS-73 touched bin/check-org.js, lib/personnel.js, public/org-chart.js and three test files, none of which this branch touches. I did not merge master into the branch: that is the orchestrator's call, and it would pull board state onto a task branch.

F-3 (minor, for whoever repeats the mutations) — node's summary repeats a failing name under `failing tests:`, so `grep -c '^✖'` returns 3 for one failing case. Cardinality by distinct name is 1, and `ℹ fail 1` agrees. Count distinct names, not marker lines.

ACCEPTANCE SWEEP — floor check only; the findings above are outside it.

1. PASS. `grep -c` in test/stream.test.js: old name "close() clears the loop poll timer as well as the heartbeat" = 0; new name "stream: AS-27/AS-80 — close() clears every interval the server armed, the loop poll included" = 1. Passes unmodified (host run below).
2. PASS. M1 (delete the `clearInterval(loopPoll)` line), whole suite, 31 files: tests 480 / pass 479 / fail 1; failing set = {T1} exactly — one distinct ✖ name, exactly as predicted, neither wider nor narrower. T1's message: `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: close() left 1 interval(s) armed`. The AS-25 close/reap case and the other two AS-27 stream cases stayed green, which is the finding this task fixes. Runner exited on its own. Site-anchored assert (AS-95 sharpening): needle occurrence 1 -> 0 at line 1074 (`clearInterval(loopPoll); // AS-27: same reason as the heartbeat above`), the close() slice between `clearInterval(heartbeat);` and `clearInterval(lanesPoll);` no longer contains `loopPoll`, the arming site `const loopPoll = setInterval(` still occurs once, and exactly one line was removed.
3. PASS. M2 (delete `clearInterval(heartbeat);`, line 1073), narrowed run `--test-name-pattern 'AS-80' test/stream.test.js` only. Control on the unmutated file: tests 1 / pass 1 (the pattern matches exactly one case). Mutated: tests 1 / pass 0 / fail 1, exit 1, no signal — the runner exited on its own rather than timing out — message `close() left 1 interval(s) armed`. Whole suite deliberately NOT run under M2, per plan §6.
4. PASS. `ids.length === 4` is asserted (with the four timer names in the message) before the inclusion check. Falsifier held: under BOTH mutants the count stayed 4 and the red came from the inclusion check — the step-4 message "update this number AND close() together" appears in neither observed output.
5. PASS. Source order: both `t.mock.method(globalThis, ...)` calls precede `createChatServer`, and `const ids = armed.mock.calls.map((c) => c.result)` is the statement immediately after it, before the first `await` (the only intervening calls are sync: mkdtempSync/loopDataDir/t.after).
6. PASS. `git diff --stat master...feat/AS-80-close-clears-every-interval` = `apps/chat/test/stream.test.js | 46 ++++---`, 1 file changed, 37 insertions, 9 deletions. No server.js, no package.json, no .lattice/.
7. PARTIAL — see F-1. Host: 480 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped. Compose, counted, scratch project `-p as80test` so production's project is untouched: exit 0, receipt ` Image as80test-test Built`, then `ℹ tests 480 / ℹ pass 480 / ℹ fail 0`. Scratch network removed afterwards (`docker compose -p as80test down --remove-orphans` -> "Network as80test_default Removed"), per the AS-106 address-pool hazard. The counts are what the plan asked for on the host; the compose figure is 480, not the 478 the criterion predicts, for the reason in F-1.
8. PASS. sha256 of server.js identical before and after each mutation (bbf7640990c30168d7cc26cef9cfc486364ca633873afee94e3fe2ee3e865b08 both times), `git -C .worktrees/AS-80 status --porcelain` empty after each restore, and the post-restore whole-suite run green at 480/480 after each. Backup + try/finally restore stands in for the shell trap.

LEFT UNDONE / for the reviewer
- AC-7's expected compose number needs re-deriving (F-1); I did not edit the plan.
- The branch's base gap (F-2) is the orchestrator's call, not mine.
- M6 probing is Ruben's, untouched by me — plan §10 names two probes (clear one handle twice while skipping another; arm a fifth interval and check the count pin reds first). I ran neither, so neither is pre-anchored.
- The M2 caveat property (a leaked ref'd heartbeat wedges the whole-file runner, plan §9) is unchanged and out of scope here.
- Artifacts: scratchpad/developer-lena/AS-80/ (host.txt, compose.txt, m1.mjs + m1-observed.txt, m2.mjs + m2-control.txt + m2-observed.txt, diff-names.mjs, progress.md).
